Quarto ships Bootstrap Icons and Font Awesome, which is a few thousand icons.
[Iconify](https://iconify.design) collects over two hundred thousand, from more than a hundred sets, behind one naming scheme.

`iconify` puts them behind one shortcode: {{< iconify octicon:rocket-16 >}} `{{{< iconify octicon:rocket-16 >}}}` draws that rocket, in HTML and in Typst alike.

The glyphs in this site's footer are drawn by it.

## Installation

```bash
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

Or install it from your editor with [Quarto Wizard](https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-wizard):

::: {.btn-group role="group" aria-label="Quarto Wizard installer options"}

[Visual Studio Code](vscode://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in Visual Studio Code using the Quarto Wizard extension."}
[Positron](positron://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in Positron using the Quarto Wizard extension."}
[VSCodium](vscodium://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in VSCodium using the Quarto Wizard extension."}

:::

## Quick start

Name the set and the icon, either way round:

```markdown
{{{< iconify octicon:rocket-16 >}}}
{{{< iconify octicon rocket-16 >}}}
```

Both draw {{< iconify octicon:rocket-16 >}}.

Size, rotate, colour, and label it with attributes:

```markdown
{{{< iconify mdi:home size=2x >}}}
{{{< iconify mdi:home rotate=90deg label="Home" >}}}
```

{{< iconify mdi:home size=2x >}} and {{< iconify mdi:home rotate=90deg label="Home" >}}.

Set a default icon set so the set can be dropped:

```yaml
extensions:
  iconify:
    set: octicon
```

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for every option, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for the attributes rendered.

## Where it works

HTML formats that run JavaScript, and Typst.
EPUB and every other format render nothing.

In HTML the icon is a web component fetched from the Iconify CDN, with a local fallback.
For Typst the SVG is retrieved once and cached, so a build repeats without the network; the [Reference](reference.qmd#typst-output) covers the cache.
